purpose: Roflumilast is used to help prevent flare-ups (called exacerbations) in people with severe COPD, especially those who have chronic bronchitis and frequent episodes of worsening symptoms. It is not a rescue inhaler and will not help during an acute attack. It works alongside your other COPD medicines to help keep your breathing more stable over time.
how_it_works: Inside your lungs, there is a chemical process that causes inflammation and makes COPD worse. Roflumilast blocks a specific enzyme called PDE4, which helps reduce that inflammation. Think of it like turning down the volume on the irritation happening in your airways, so your lungs work a little better and flare-ups happen less often.
common_side_effects: Diarrhea, nausea, stomach pain, headache, decreased appetite, weight loss, trouble sleeping, and dizziness are the most commonly reported side effects. These often improve after the first few weeks of taking the medication.
warnings: This medicine can cause significant weight loss, so your doctor will monitor your weight regularly. It should not be used if you have moderate to severe liver problems. Some people have experienced mood changes, depression, or thoughts of self-harm — contact your doctor right away if you notice any changes in your mood or behavior. Tell your doctor about all medicines you take, as some can interact with roflumilast.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 500 microgram (0.5 mg) tablet taken by mouth once daily, with or without food. Some doctors may start you on a lower dose of 250 mcg once daily for the first four weeks to help reduce stomach-related side effects, then increase to the full dose.
